note_on_method: Each venue page rests on two City of Kirkland pages (the pickleball page that counts the courts, and the park's own page that gives the address and the detail) plus the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. Where the City says nothing, these pages say that it says nothing.

slots.description:
Six dedicated pickleball courts on the edge of downtown Kirkland. The City documented the changeover on this park's own page: the tennis courts "closed on Monday, April 13, 2026 for conversion to six dedicated pickleball courts", and "The new pickleball courts opened July 2, 2026 at 3 p.m."

Dedicated is the City's word. Most of what this directory publishes is a tennis court carrying a second set of lines, where the net is the wrong height and half the paint is for a different game. These are not that.

The park also has a lighted baseball field, a skate park, a basketball court, a seasonal swimming pool and the Peter Kirk Community Center, with the Kirkland Performance Center, Library and Transit Center next door.
slots.getting_there: 202 3rd St, Kirkland, WA 98033, in King County. The City says "Parking is available in the Municipal Parking Garage or along Central Way." It does not say what the garage charges. The Kirkland Transit Center is next door, so this is the easiest of the three Kirkland venues to reach without driving. There is a year-round restroom on the west side of the park, and the City says public Wi-Fi is available.
slots.what_to_expect:
Six courts, open 8 a.m. to dusk daily, drop-in use only and first-come, first-served. You cannot book one, and Kirkland prohibits business use of its pickleball courts, including lessons, leagues and tournaments.

The six are split by position. The three nearest the skate park are open play: if all three are full and players are waiting, play one game to 11 points and rotate off. The three nearest the street are timed: when full with players waiting, limit play to 30 minutes and rotate.

Lighting is not stated, and the dusk closing time means there is no lit evening session. The lighted baseball field is not a lit court. The surface is not stated, though whatever it is was laid in 2026.

faqs.a: Six, and they are dedicated pickleball courts. The park's own page states "Peter Kirk Park has six pickleball courts and one basketball court", and the City's pickleball page lists "6 pickleball courts".
No. They are drop-in use only and first-come, first-served.

slots.description:
Three pickleball courts in a community park south-east of downtown, alongside ballfields, a playground, a picnic shelter and restrooms that the City replaced in 2026.

All three courts are open play. The City states: "The pickleball courts are available for drop in use only." The posted rotation rule is the simple one: if the courts are full and players are waiting, play one game to 11 points and rotate off.

The count of three comes from Kirkland's pickleball page, which lists "3 pickleball courts" here. The park's own page mentions its pickleball courts several times and never says how many there are. Nothing contradicts the figure, but it rests on one City record rather than two.
slots.getting_there:
500 8th St S, Kirkland, WA 98033, in King County.

This is the best-documented parking of any venue on this site, and the credit belongs entirely to the City for writing it down: "There are two parking lots at Everest with space for up to 100 vehicles." The City does not say whether parking costs anything or when it fills, and a park with ballfields can fill for reasons that have nothing to do with pickleball. There are year-round restrooms.
slots.what_to_expect:
Three open-play courts, 8 a.m. to dusk, every day, free of any charge the City mentions - though note that it never actually says the courts are free, so this site does not claim it. The "Free Play" heading on this park's page is field time on the grass and synthetic turf, offered March to October and year-round respectively. It is about the fields, not the courts.

You cannot book a court. Kirkland runs its classes and leagues elsewhere and prohibits business use of its pickleball courts.

Lighting is not stated, and with a dusk closing time there is no evening session to light. The surface is not stated, and this venue carries no renovation date to hint at its age.

faqs.a: No. The courts are drop-in use only and first-come, first-served across the whole city.
8 a.m. to dusk, daily, the same as every Kirkland pickleball court.

slots.description:
One pickleball court. The City's pickleball page lists "1 pickleball court" here, and the park's own page calls it "a 44-foot pickleball court". Forty-four feet is the regulation length of one court, so the two records agree.

The City says the park "was renovated and expanded by Google and SRM Development in 2021-2022". The court arrived as part of that work alongside a 16-foot-wide paved trail, an urban farm growing vegetables for Hopelink, a splash area, a zip-line, a sand volleyball court, a basketball court, a grass amphitheatre and year-round bathrooms.

One court means one game. If it is taken when you arrive, there is no second court to move to.
slots.getting_there: 509 6th Street South, Kirkland, WA 98033, in King County, the same postcode as the other two Kirkland venues. The City lists a parking lot among this park's amenities and does not say how large it is. There are bathrooms, open year-round.
slots.what_to_expect:
One court, 8 a.m. to dusk, drop-in and first-come, first-served. No booking, and no lessons, leagues or tournaments: the City prohibits business use on all of its pickleball courts.

The City posts its specific rotation rules at Everest and Peter Kirk and not at this park, which is consistent with a single court but is not a statement that no rule applies.

Lighting is not stated and the court closes at dusk. The surface is not stated. The court is part of a park rebuilt in 2021-2022, so it is not old.

faqs.a: No. It is drop-in use only and first-come, first-served.
Not stated by the City, and the court is open only from 8 a.m. to dusk.
